page.notes: Greek word after "& " (between "Pontifices iniusta," and "& praeter ius") is printed in a different, smaller hand and is not legible enough to transcribe; the placeholder stands in its place. The "sediū" tilde is read as an abbreviation for -um. Printed page number 63 is read from the top right; the scan is slightly skewed. Line-end hyphen in "alio-" continues on the next page. Some letters of the first line are faint (e.g. "annes?" is a fragment carried over from the previous page).
